rationale: Validation status is fail and analyzer status is fail, so the case cannot be retained despite mutation_score=0.833 and coverage_score=1.0 meeting thresholds. Two independent issues were flagged: (1) a public_security_leak in metadata.json, which explicitly names CWE-208, CWE-200, and CWE-385 in the metrics descriptions, revealing hidden security intent to participants; and (2) a dead_check/uncovered_requirement on SR3, whose static scan is narrowly anchored to the exact baseline pattern 'if (key[i] == 0) { ... return; }' and never independently fails any other mutant, providing zero discrimination beyond the shipped baseline.
revision_instructions: Two fixes are required. First, strip the CWE identifiers (CWE-208, CWE-200, CWE-385) and any other hidden-security-revealing language from metadata.json's metrics descriptions -- replace with generic phrasing such as 'targeted security properties' or 'information-flow non-interference between secret and public outputs' so the baseline and metadata read as ordinary functional artifacts, not as a marked vulnerability challenge. Quote paths flagged: metadata.json (public_security_leak: mentions CWE-200, CWE-208, CWE-385). Second, broaden the SR3 static scan in evaluation/evaluate.py so it is not solely anchored to the literal baseline construct 'if (key[i] == 0) { *status = ERR_KEY_ZERO_BYTE; ... return; }'. The check must FAIL when it detects ANY key-dependent early-exit pattern in the submission -- generalize matching to cover variant forms such as different comparison operators (key[i]!=0), different variable/array names, switch/case constructs, nested conditionals, or early break/continue keyed on key content -- while still PASSing on the golden's unconditional single for-loop over len with no branch on key values. Add at least one additional mutant that reintroduces a key-dependent early exit using different syntax/naming than the shipped baseline, and confirm SR3 now emits [TEST] FAIL on that mutant to prove real discriminative value (currently SR3 never fires FAIL on any mutant, per dead_checks and uncovered_requirements in the validation report).
